# Safety board: motorless bench tests (generated by `python -m rnd.safety_board_sim`)

**Step-1 gate (M1_READINESS exit criterion 1):** every test below passes on the built board, with no motor connected, before any drive is powered from it. Numbers come from the simulation ([safety_board_sim.md](safety_board_sim.md)) with tolerances; a reading outside the pass band stops the build until it is understood. Record every scope capture (PNG + CSV) in docs/sw/board_tests/ with the date and the board revision.

## Equipment

- Bench supply: the SE-1000-24 set to **24.0 V** (Fable #2 minor: at 25.2 V the clamp's lowest turn-off, 25.44 V, is only 0.24 V away against the supply's ± 1 % and 150 mV ripple, and a drift makes the clamp chop against the supply; 24.0 V leaves ≈ 1 V; the simulation's 25.2 V full pack stays the worst case for the regen numbers) (and the 0–30 V / 10 A CC supply for T0 and T9); a second CC supply (0–30 V) for the clamp tests.
- **Dummy drive load:** a capacitor bank of 2.35 mF (5 × 470 µF 35 V, the M1 drivers' input capacitance) on 0.5 m of 14 AWG at the end of the real 1.5 m arm lead + F3, plus switchable resistors: 10 Ω 50 W (RH-50, pre-charge fault), 5.6 Ω and 2.2 Ω 50 W on the heatsink.
- **Regen source:** the 0–30 V / 20 A CC supply in series with a **40 A Schottky** (Vishay VS-40CPQ060-N3, 60 V, both 20 A legs in parallel, on a small heatsink: ≈ 0.5 V × 30 A ≈ 15 W for 200 ms; the 1N5822 named before is a 3 A part) into the dummy drive bank (it pushes current *into* the bus, which the SE-1000 cannot sink); ≈ 500 W of simulated regen. **The 20 A supply cannot make T12's 30 A step:** the extra 10 A comes from the energy bank (T12). Energy bank: 22 mF 50 V, charged to 30 V for the dumps (9.9 J … repeat 10× in 1 s for the pulse duty) and to 32.5 V for the 30 A step, switched in through 0.33 Ω and a second VS-40CPQ060-N3.
- 4-channel scope (≥ 100 MHz, 1 GS/s) with ×10 passive probes (≥ 300 V) and ground springs: **no differential probe** (Fable #2 minor: Q1–Q3, Q4 and Q5 are low-side switches, so every drain is measured to board ground, and the SE-1000 output floats), a 100 A DC current clamp (**≥ 500 kHz**: the Micsig CP2100A's 800 kHz is enough, see *Current-clamp bandwidth* below) and a 30 A clamp; a function generator (3.3 V square, 250 Hz = the 500 Hz heartbeat toggle) for GPIO17; a thermocouple on the resistor plate; DMM; a stopwatch log (the scope timebase is the reference, not any software timestamp).
- Scope points: **TP1 VBUS at the board**, **TP2 VBUS at the dummy drive bank** (end of the arm lead), **TP3 Q1 drain** (×10 probe, ground spring on Q1's source), **TP4 Q1 gate**, TP5 WD_OK, TP6 Q4 gate, **TP7 Q4 drain**, TP8 AUX_RAW (opto output), TP9 FORCE, TP10 LATCH, TP11 K2_DRIVE, **TP12 AUX_DB** (debounced), **TP13 RUN**; current: clamp leg 1, supply lead, K1 coil.

## Tests (pass / fail)

| # | Test | Setup and stimulus | Measure | Pass | Fail → |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T0 | First power, logic only | CC supply at 24.0 V / 1 A limit, no load, no heartbeat | supply current; 12 V and 3.3 V rails; LATCH | ≤ 0.15 A; 12 V ± 5 %, 3.3 V ± 3 %; LATCH 0, K1 and K2 open | stop: rails / shorts |
| T1 | Power-on comes up disarmed | supply off → on 10 times, heartbeat running, ARM not pressed; then 5 times with ARM held down during power-up | LATCH, K1, K2 (TP10, AUX) | LATCH stays 0 every time (R9·C9 POR ≥ 50 ms on TP10) | POR network |
| T2 | ARM refused | (a) a mushroom pressed (each one, each channel); (b) no heartbeat; (c) TH1 open (unplug); (d) **AUX forced high** (short the opto output) with the fix | LATCH after SB1 | LATCH stays 0 in every case | U10 D gating |
| T3 | Pre-charge into the dummy bank | heartbeat on, ARM; dummy bank 2.35 mF + board 4.7 mF; measure the real idle draw first (drives' logic boards if available) | TP1/TP2 rise, K2 / K1 timing, supply current; **AUX bounce**: TP8 + TP12 at 500 µs/div (single shot on TP8 rising) on 20 closings | PRE_OK at 59 ms ± 30 % (τ = 23 ms); inrush ≤ 8.4 A; K1 closes ≤ 94 ms after ARM with ΔV ≤ 1.6 V; K2 open ≤ 12 ms after TP8 first closes (t_stable ≤ 5.7 ms + K2 release); idle draw × 3.3 Ω ≤ 2.0 V; bounce burst ≤ 3 ms with no closed interval > 1.2 ms, and one clean TP12 edge per closing (else re-size C_db: design change 10) | pre-charge / PRE_OK divider / debounce |
| T4 | Pre-charge fault | 10 Ω RH-50 across VBUS, ARM | TP1, LATCH, K2, R3 temperature | bus settles ≈ 18.4 V (< VIN − 3 V), K1 never closes, PRE_TIMEOUT clears LATCH at 1.0 s ± 0.2 s, K2 opens; R3 ≤ 20 J; FORCE (TP9) fires exactly once, as K2_DRIVE falls (the SN74LVC1G123's CLR̄ ↑ trigger), never before | U11 timer |
| T5 | Watchdog timeout | armed, running; stop the 250 Hz square at a random phase (20 runs); also 3 runs each at 4 / 8 / 12 ms edge spacing (must not trip) | last edge → WD_OK low (TP5) → Q4 gate (TP6) → AUX (TP8) | WD_OK low 22.5–30.0 ms after the last edge (25 ms ± 10 % with a C0G cap; the design allows ± 20 %); no trip at ≤ 12 ms spacing | R4/C3; if over 30 ms the SW2 budget fails |
| T6 | Contactor release | as T5; K1 coil current clamp + Q4 drain (TP7); repeat 20× | Q4 off → AUX open; Q4 drain peak | release ≤ 10 ms; **TP7 ≤ 80 % of Q4's V_DS** (≈ 50 V expected with D1 + Z1: needs the 100 V part, design change 1) | suppression / Q4 rating |
| T7 | Forced discharge one-shot | armed with the dummy bank; open by heartbeat stop, by each mushroom, by TH1, and **uncommanded** by unplugging the K1 coil | FORCE (TP9) width, TP1/TP2 → 10 V, TP11 K2_DRIVE, TP13 RUN | FORCE fires on every opening ≤ 1 ms after TP8 opens (simulated 0.5 ms on the coil unplug), width 100 ms ± 20 %; TP2 (far end) < 10 V ≤ 4 ms after TP8 (simulated 2.0 ms); on the coil unplug TP11 stays low and K2 never re-closes (netlist v4; v3 re-closed it and fired FORCE only at the 30 ms discrepancy); FORCE never fires while K2_DRIVE is high (T3) | U6 (Ā = AUX_DB, CLR̄), U28 RUN, U29 debounce |
| T8 | End-to-end stop time | heartbeat stopped (a hung loop) with the dummy bank charged and a 2.2 Ω load at TP2 standing in for a drive | last heartbeat edge → TP2 < 10 V and load current < 0.5 A (independent of software timestamps) | ≤ 50 ms in 20/20 runs (simulated worst 45.5 ms) | watchdog / release / discharge |
| T9 | No self re-arm | (a) tap a mushroom for < 50 ms while armed; (b) unplug and replug the K1 coil while armed; (c) restore the heartbeat after T5; (d) supply off/on | LATCH, K1, K2, TP11 | after each: LATCH 0, K1 and K2 stay open until SB1 is pressed again; in (b) TP11 never goes high | U10 CLR̄ terms, U28 |
| T10 | Clamp threshold and hysteresis | CC supply (no SE-1000) into VBUS through 1 Ω, ramp 24 → 28 V at 1 V/s | TP4 gate on / off levels at TP1 | on 26.00 V ± 1 %, off 25.70 V ± 1 % (never on below 25.5 V) | divider / TL431 |
| T11 | Clamp switching edge | regen source 20 A into TP2, clamp chopping | TP3 drain overshoot, TP4 gate edge, freewheel current | TP3 ≤ 48 V (simulated 28.1 V); gate edge 0.2–0.5 µs; no ringing > 5 V after 1 µs | layout loop / R_G / diode |
| T12 | Regen at the drive | regen source at TP2: 10 and 20 A steps for 200 ms from the 20 A supply; **30 A = the 20 A supply + the 22 mF bank at 32.5 V through 0.33 Ω** (15 → 10 A extra over 2.9 ms = 13 chopper cycles at the simulated 4.5 kHz; the drive-end voltage settles within the first cycles, so read the 30 A point in that window); then the bank at 30 V dumped into TP2 10× in 1 s | TP1 and **TP2** max, resistor plate temperature | TP2 ≤ 27.1 V at 24 A (the 611 W regen limit; simulated 26.79 V at the lead end, 27.47 V at the elbow at 598 W); chopper 1–20 kHz, never MHz bursts on TP4; plate ≤ 60 °C after the 10 dumps; TH1 opens at 85 °C ± 5 (heat gun) | filter / on-time / regen limit (design changes 0, 5) |
| T13 | Loss of clamp power | armed, running; pull F2 (12 V / 3.3 V logic) for 1 s | K1, LATCH, TP4 | K1 opens (WD_OK has no supply), board comes back disarmed; with design change 4: 12 V UVLO opens K1 before the 3.3 V rail falls | UVLO |
| T14 | AUX faults | (a) cut the AUX opto wire while running; (b) short the AUX opto output while stopped and press ARM; (c) while running, open the aux loop for 0.1 ms (a MOSFET in series driven by the function generator) 20 times | K1, FORCE, supply current, TP12 | (a) stop: FORCE ≤ 1 ms after the cut (the AUX_DB edge; simulated 0.5 ms), K1 opens ≤ 12 ms (the supply may latch: acceptable); (b) ARM refused (design change 2); (c) TP12 never moves, no FORCE, still armed (glitches < 0.17 ms are ignored) | AUX logic / debounce |
| T15 | Welded K1 (simulated) | replace K1's main contact with a 10 AWG link (coil still driven), stop the heartbeat | FORCE, supply state | design change 3 / 10: FORCE 36–44 ms after Q4 off, the SE-1000 latches off (power removed) | discrepancy monitor |
| T16 | Supply trip | with the dummy bank and 2.2 Ω, raise the load until the SE-1000 trips (≥ 43.8 A) | board state after the trip and after re-power | board disarmed after re-power (T1); no fuse operated; wiring ≤ 60 °C | POR / wiring |

Order: T0–T2 at 1 A current limit; T3–T9 on the SE-1000 with the dummy bank; T10–T12 with the CC regen source; T13–T16 last. Only then does the first drive (Step 1) get power, with the catch cradle set (electrical.md *Category-0 drop protection*).

**Robot board only (base channel, §6 of safety_board_sim.md):** before the base is powered; not part of the Step-1 gate (the M1 bench has no base).

| # | Test | Setup and stimulus | Measure | Pass | Fail → |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T17 | Base SS1 delay (U20) | base channel populated, a 1.9 mF dummy bank (4 × 470 µF) + 2.2 Ω on VBUS_B; armed; stop by each mushroom (each of its channels c, d), by the arm heartbeat, by the base heartbeat (GPIO23); 20 runs | K1 AUX, Q9 enable, VBUS_B, U20 contacts | K1 opens ≤ 10 ms on a mushroom while Q9 stays on; Q9 off 1.8–2.2 s after the stop (U20 set 2.0 s; the longest software ramp is 1.6 s); heartbeats restored during the delay do not cancel it; only ARM re-enables; ARM refused without the base heartbeat | U20 setting / wiring, WD_B |
| T18 | Base clamp leg and FORCE_B | CC supply into VBUS_B through 1 Ω (ramp 24 → 28 V at 1 V/s); then a T17 stop with the dummy bank charged | Q10 gate on / off at VBUS_B; FORCE_B width; far end of the dummy bank | on 26.00 V ± 1 %, off 25.70 V ± 1 %; FORCE_B 100 ms ± 20 % on every Q9 opening; dummy bank < 10 V ≤ 3 ms after Q9 off (simulated 1.5 ms) | base comparator / U25 |
| T19 | Shorted base switch, soft-start, caster feed | (a) link across Q9, T17 stop; (b) ARM into the empty dummy bank; (c) the caster release (one 55 N JF-1264B pull solenoid pulling the 4 lock plates through Ø1 cables (D29 #9)) on VBUS_B, released, then a T17 stop | DISC_B, supply current, VBUS_B rise, solenoid current | (a) DISC_B 50 ms ± 20 % after the enable drops; (b) inrush ≤ 12 A, VBUS_B rises in ≈ 50 ms; (c) solenoid current ≈ 1.1 A (ESTIMATE) while released; it drops (all four casters lock) when Q9 opens and never before it while the Pi holds it released | LM5069 / DISC_B / caster feed |

## Current-clamp bandwidth (which clamp each test needs)

The sheet asked for ≥ 1 MHz on the 100 A clamp; the BOM's Micsig CP2100A is DC–800 kHz (first-order rise ≈ 0.44 µs, time constant 0.20 µs). No pass / fail line reads a current edge: edges are timed on voltages (TP3/TP4 with the 100 MHz probe). What the clamp must read is the amplitude of each current event, which the simulation's own time scales set:

| Test | Current read | Fastest feature (simulation) | CP2100A reads | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T3 | pre-charge inrush (supply lead) | RC decay τ = 23 ms | 100 % | ✅ |
| T6 | K1 coil current to drop-out | 1.6 ms decay | 100 % | ✅ |
| T7 | forced discharge, clamp leg 1 (≈ 41 A) | RC decay τ = 1.3 ms | 100 % | ✅ |
| T11 / T12 | clamp leg 1 on-pulses (≈ 44 A) | ≥ 50 µs flat top (min on-time; chopper 4.5 kHz) | 100 % | ✅ |
| T11 | freewheel diode current after turn-off | L/R decay τ = 1.8 µs (NH-50 1 µH / 0.56 Ω) | 76 % | ⚠️ informational only |
| T16 | supply lead at the SE-1000 trip | the supply's ms shutdown | 100 % | ✅ |

**Verdict: 800 kHz is enough; the requirement becomes ≥ 500 kHz.** The only feature it cannot follow is the freewheel diode's µs decay in T11, which no pass line uses: the freewheel peak equals the leg current at turn-off (the resistor's inductance keeps the current continuous), and that is read on the ≥ 50 µs flat top. A CP2100B (2.5 MHz, ≈ €699) is not needed.

## Review gate G-SB: independent schematic + layout review (owner picks the reviewer)

**Where it sits:** after the board is drawn in KiCad and `python -m rnd.safety_board_sim` passes on the drawn values; before any Step-1b board part is ordered (M1_READINESS: Step 1b waits for it) and long before T0. Step 1a (the motor on a 1 A limit, no board) does not wait for it.

**What the review covers (all of it; a partial review does not close the gate):**

1. Every line of the checklist below (schematic, layout, before sign-off), signed or with a defect written against it.
2. The logic as a state machine, not gate by gate: ARM, pre-charge, run, every stop (commanded, uncommanded K1 drop-out, welded K1, stuck / broken AUX, 12 V loss, POR), each traced on the schematic with the netlist v4 race fix (RUN latch, AUX debounce, discrepancy window); the reviewer writes down any sequence the simulation's §5 does not cover.
3. The power stage: the clamp loop, the 146 A path, the freewheel diodes, Q4's drain rating, the K1 / K2 / fuse DC ratings, re-derived from the datasheets.
4. The pass / fail numbers of T0–T16 (are they the right tests, are the limits right, can the bench equipment measure them).
5. A short written verdict: build as drawn / build after the listed fixes / do not build.

**Who qualifies (any one route; never the drafter, i.e. Claude or any agent in this repo, never one reviewer alone, never an AI review: Fable, Astra and Neon are design reviews, not this gate):**

| Route | Who | Minimum qualification | Cost / time (ESTIMATE) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Hired EE review | one electrical engineer engaged for a fixed-scope review (freelance platform, a local electronics design consultancy, or a university power-electronics lab doing paid work) | degree-level EE plus ≥ 5 years designing power electronics, motor drives or machine safety circuits (a PE / CEng / IEng, or a TÜV functional-safety engineer, counts on its own); has designed a board that switches ≥ 20 A DC | 4–8 h, ≈ $400–1,200; 1–2 weeks |
| B. Maker-community review | **two** independent reviewers from a public electronics community (EEVblog forum, KiCad forum, an open-source robotics / ODrive / VESC / BMS project's contributors) | each with a public track record: a published board that switches ≥ 20 A DC or a published safety / BMS / motor-controller design, linkable; both do the whole checklist (a thread of 'looks fine' replies is not a review) | free or a small honorarium; 2–4 weeks |
| C. Bought-relay fallback | route A or B on a smaller board | as A or B | see below |
| **D. Owner + second EE (chosen, D30)** | **the owner (an electrical engineer, primary reviewer: the whole checklist) and the owner's father (an electrical engineer, second reviewer: independently, at least the power stage, clamp loop, K1/K2/fuse ratings, discharge path and the stop state machine)** | both electrical engineers; the drafter is Claude/agents, so neither reviewer drew the board | owner's time; no fee |

**Minimum evidence to accept it (all five, filed as docs/review/board_review_<date>.md with the attachments):**

1. Reviewer identity and qualification (name, route A / B / D, a link or CV line for the qualification above) and a one-line conflict statement (route D: the owner has a stake in the build, which is why the second reviewer checks the high-energy parts independently and signs separately).
2. The exact files reviewed: the KiCad project's git commit hash, and the electrical.md / safety_board_sim.md revisions.
3. This checklist with every line signed or a defect written (routes B and D: one per reviewer), plus the annotated schematic PDF or the reviewer's ERC / DRC report, so the review is visibly of the drawing and not of the prose.
4. A defect list with severity (stop / fix before build / note); every 'stop' and 'fix' closed by a commit the reviewer re-checks (a delta review of the changed sheets), or accepted in writing by the reviewer.
5. The reviewer's own re-run of `python -m rnd.safety_board_sim` on the drawn values (its summary pasted in), or a statement of which numbers they re-derived by hand instead.

**If no reviewer is found within 3 weeks of the board being drawn** (the gate must not stall Step 1 indefinitely; Fable #2 M2): route C. Move the e-stop loop, the monitored reset and the welded-contact check to a bought safety relay with monitored manual reset and contactor feedback (the G9SA family the base channel already uses), keep the custom board for the clamp, pre-charge and watchdog only, and review that smaller board by route A or B. That removes about ten single-gate ICs (U6's race path, U10, U11, U17, U28, U29 among them) and most of the logic review. The owner chooses the route and the person; this page only fixes what the review must cover and what closes it.

## Independent review checklist (schematic + layout, before the board parts are ordered)

The reviewer named under *Review gate* above signs each line (name, date) or writes the defect. The reviewer gets the KiCad project, this file, safety_board_sim.md and electrical.md's netlist; nothing is checked against a description of the board.

**Schematic**

- [ ] Every net in the electrical.md netlist exists with the same name; every pin of every IC is connected or explicitly tied (no floating CLR̄, PRE, unused gates).
- [ ] SN74LVC1G123 U5 / U6 / one-shots: trigger on the documented pin (Ā falling / B rising), CLR̄ polarity, R·C values give 25 ms / 100 ms (TI SCES586 table, C0G caps); the CLR̄ ↑ trigger (Ā low, B high) of U6 fires only at a pre-charge abort, as intended (T4).
- [ ] U10 D = S1b ∧ S2b ∧ WD_OK ∧ TH1 ∧ ¬AUX_DB (robot: ∧ WD_B); CLR̄ = ¬(STOP ∨ FORCE ∨ POR ∨ PRE_TIMEOUT ∨ DISC ∨ UV12 ∨ OC), STOP = ¬S1b ∨ ¬S2b ∨ ¬WD_OK ∨ ¬TH1 (robot: ∨ ¬WD_B); SB1 is the clock, debounced, NO (the same terms as electrical.md's netlist and nets table).
- [ ] **Netlist v4 race fix:** U28 RUN (CLK = AUX_DB ↑, CLR̄ = LATCH); K2_DRIVE = LATCH ∧ ¬RUN ∧ ¬PRE_TIMEOUT; U6 Ā, U8, U10 D, U11, U17 all on AUX_DB, nothing on AUX_RAW but U29 and GPIO27; no path by which an AUX edge changes U6's CLR̄ while LATCH is high.
- [ ] **AUX debounce U29:** R_c 100 kΩ 1 %, R_d 4.7 kΩ 1 % + BAT54, C_db 47 nF C0G, U29 74LVC1G17; BAT54 orientation (discharges C_db when AUX_RAW falls); the 74LVC1G17 thresholds at 3.3 V re-derived from the datasheet and `python -m rnd.safety_board_sim` re-run if they fall outside VT+ 1.3–2.2 V / VT− 0.6–1.5 V.
- [ ] Q4 coil driver V_DS ≥ 2 × (supply + V_Z1) and V_GS(th) specified at the driving voltage; Q5 likewise; gate pull-downs so a dead driver means off.
- [ ] D1 + Z1 orientation (Zener reverse-biased in normal operation, diode blocks the supply); coil suppression on K2 too.
- [ ] Mushroom channel 1 in series with the coil on the **high side** of the coil, channel 2 only to logic; both NC; wiring diagram shows both buttons.
- [ ] TLV3202 divider: 0.1 % resistors, the hysteresis resistor, the 2 µs RC (design change 0); reference TL431B decoupled; PRE_OK compares VBUS with VIN (not with a fixed level).
- [ ] U16 minimum on-time (50 µs, triggered by OV ↑) ORed with OV and FORCE before the UCC27524; nothing else can hold the gate on.
- [ ] U17 discrepancy monitor: XOR(Q4 gate, AUX_DB), RC 40 ms ± 10% (> operate 25 ms + bounce + t_stable = 33.7 ms; < 50 ms), into U6's trigger and U10's CLR̄.
- [ ] U18 12 V UVLO and U19 branch-current trip (16 A, 5 s) into U10's CLR̄; F3 still in series for shorts.
- [ ] Robot board: the base branch is fed by Q9 from VIN, **not** from VBUS after K1; Q9's enable only through U20's two OFF-delay contacts in series; U20's input on the mushrooms' own NC blocks (c, d) + the LATCH photoMOS; WD_B into U10's CLR̄ and D; the caster-release solenoid on VBUS_B; the base clamp leg and FORCE_B on VBUS_B and nowhere else (no diode from VBUS_B to VBUS).
- [ ] UCC27524 supply from U2 with the 12 V UVLO into the coil chain; gate resistors per MOSFET; Kelvin source not required but source returns to the film cap.
- [ ] Freewheel Schottky across **each** NH-50 (anode at the drain, cathode at VBUS); IFSM, V_RRM ≥ 60 V.
- [ ] Ideal diode U1/Q6 orientation (blocks VBUS → PSU), its gate supply, reverse-recovery behaviour on a fast regen edge.
- [ ] Logic supply U2/U3 from VIN through F2 and nothing else on it; the Pi's ground and the board ground meet at one point; optos on AUX and ESTOP_SENSE.
- [ ] Power-on reset R9·C9 holds LATCH cleared ≥ 50 ms after 3.3 V is valid; brown-out below 2.5 V clears it too.
- [ ] DC ratings: K1 (ALEV100) breaking 100 A at 28 V DC with its polarity marked; K2 contact 10 A DC at 30 V; fuses DC-rated for the pack's short-circuit current (MIDI, ATO).
- [ ] Every rating in electrical.md's tables re-derived from the datasheets by the reviewer (MOSFET SOA at 49 A / 100 ms, NH-50 pulse rating, TVS, capacitor ripple at the chopper frequency).

**Layout**

- [ ] Clamp loop (film cap → NH-50 leads → diode → MOSFET → source → film cap) area minimised: ≤ 30 nH estimated (≤ 15 mm × 15 mm loop on a 2-layer board, or short bus bars).
- [ ] 146 A path: copper width/thickness or bus bars sized for 49 A per leg pulses and ≈ 15 A continuous; temperature rise ≤ 20 K; 10 AWG lugs crimped, not soldered.
- [ ] High-current return does not share copper with the comparator divider, the TL431 or the logic ground (star point at C1).
- [ ] Divider sense point is the VBUS terminal, Kelvin-connected; trace away from the switching node.
- [ ] Creepage/clearance ≥ 1 mm between VBUS and logic; optos straddle a clear gap.
- [ ] NH-50s on an aluminium plate with TH1 on the same plate; thermal pad; plate grounded or insulated by design.
- [ ] Test points TP1–TP11 accessible with a scope ground spring; current-clamp loops on leg 1, supply lead and K1 coil.
- [ ] Connectors keyed (no swapping the e-stop loop with the heartbeat); strain relief on the 10 AWG leads.

**Before sign-off**

- [ ] The reviewer re-ran `python -m rnd.safety_board_sim` on the drawn values and every ✅ above still holds; any change goes back into electrical.md.
- [ ] The design changes listed in safety_board_sim.md are in the schematic, or the reviewer accepts the risk in writing.
